title: Singapore-flagged GFS Pride sinks in Hormuz after projectile strike
summary: The Singapore-registered container ship GFS Pride sank in the Strait of Hormuz after being struck by an unidentified projectile; all 21 crew were evacuated uninjured (Singapore MPA). UKMTO had reported the attack Tuesday; sister ship GFS Giselle was damaged. IRGC claimed a naval mine on an 'unauthorised' route; maritime firm Marisks said there is no independent evidence of mining. Reuters quoted Iranian officials saying Tehran is changing shipping tactics to keep oil prices high ahead of the Nov 3 US midterms. More than 20 vessels have been attacked this month in Hormuz, the Gulf and Gulf of Oman (UKMTO).

analysis.text: Stated motive is enforcing Iran's transit rules after the US blockade; real leverage is midterm oil-price pressure and forcing Washington to trade sanctions/blockade relief for shipping safety. Expanding beyond tankers to containers raises insurance and rerouting costs globally.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct surge in Iranian strikes on commercial shipping

title: Ukraine ends energy pause; Zelenskyy says 'we're done' with Trump ceasefire
summary: President Zelenskyy told the Financial Times Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian oil refineries after a three-day pause requested by Washington. He said Russia struck Ukrainian energy infrastructure (Kyiv cited ~40 ballistic missiles in one assault) while Ukraine held fire. Russia said Ukraine hit a Ryazan-region refinery early Thursday. Zelenskyy also cited alleged limits on Starlink/Starshield mobility and reduced missile-warning intel; SpaceX's Musk said Starshield is US-government controlled. Trump's Sunday 'energy ceasefire' was tied to a US purchase of Russian diesel meant to ease US fuel prices before midterms.

analysis.text: Stated US goal was protecting energy infrastructure and cutting fuel prices; actual bargain mixed a diesel import deal with Moscow and pressure on Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refining. Collapse raises diesel/oil risk again and deepens Kyiv–Washington trust fracture ahead of Nov 3.

causes.why: Unilateral US energy ceasefire announcement failed when Russia kept striking Ukrainian energy and Kyiv ended its pause
US–Russia diesel deal was the political quid for pressing Kyiv to halt refinery strikes

revisions.why: Place today's story: Reuters/AP name the Rosneft refinery in Ryazan as the target hit.

title: Saudi coalition says cruise missile intercepted over Medina; Houthis keep targeting oil and airports
summary: On Oct 15 the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a cruise missile over the Medina region; Houthis called the claim a lie. On Oct 14 Houthis vowed more attacks on Saudi airports and oil after a strike that sources said heavily damaged Aramco's Dhahran HQ (Saudi Energy Ministry: limited fire). Riyadh King Khalid airport was hit Oct 10 (13 killed). Saudi-led strikes hit Sanaa-area fuel sites. Houthis swept to Bab el-Mandeb in September; Saudi-backed forces later pressed toward Mokha.

analysis.text: Stated Houthi motive is retaliation for Saudi strikes in Yemen; as Iran's proxy they open a second chokepoint (Bab el-Mandeb) while Hormuz burns, multiplying oil and Red Sea shipping risk without Tehran owning every shot.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct Houthi campaign against Saudi oil and airports
Same Iran-linked Gulf crisis: Hormuz pressure plus Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb second front

revisions.why: Place today's story at the named sites: Medina intercept, Dhahran HQ, Riyadh airport.

title: Kabila's FRN dissolves AFC/M23 umbrella, claims Doha peace commitments
summary: In a Goma statement dated Oct 14, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) led by ex-president Joseph Kabila said it had dissolved the Congo River Alliance (AFC) and assumed AFC's rights and Doha-process obligations. FRN was launched Oct 12 with M23 figures (incl. Sultani Makenga) as deputies. UN envoy Huang Xia told the Security Council a 'window of opportunity' remains via US- and Qatar-led tracks; illicit mineral trade still funds armed groups. M23 still holds Rubaya (~15% of world coltan).

analysis.text: Stated aim is national refoundation and honoring Doha; actual move consolidates Kabila's open leadership of the Rwanda-accused M23 mineral machine while keeping a diplomatic off-ramp. US–DRC minerals pact and AI/electronics demand make Rubaya leverage real.

causes.why: FRN is the formal successor structure to the Oct 12 Kabila–M23 coalition announcement

revisions.why: FRN statement was issued in Goma.

title: Taiwan tracks 15 PLA aircraft and 10 PLAN ships; median-line crossings continue
summary: Taiwan's MND reported that from 06:00 Oct 14 to 06:00 Oct 15 it tracked 15 PLA aircraft, 10 PLAN ships and seven official ships; 13 aircraft crossed the median line into northern, central, southwestern and eastern ADIZ sectors. On Oct 14 alone it had reported 13 sorties with 11 median-line crossings during a 'joint combat readiness patrol.' China's announced live-fire window runs Oct 12–17.

analysis.text: Stated PLA framing is routine combat readiness; pressure after Lai's speech keeps Taiwan and US allies reacting while China retains rare-earth and chip-supply leverage into the Nov 10 control-suspension date.

causes.why: Continuation of the Oct 12–17 live-fire / readiness patrol cycle after Lai's speech

title: Houthi missiles hit Aden presidential palace, killing five
summary: Houthis fired missiles and drones at Aden's Al-Maashiq presidential palace complex, seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, killing five and wounding 16 (Yemeni health minister). The PM and cabinet were safe. It is the first strike on the palace in the current Houthi-Saudi conflict. The coalition said Houthis made 20 attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid airport this month (17 killed, 333 wounded); ICAO's council condemned attacks on Saudi civil aviation.

causes.why: Escalation of the Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies

analysis.text: Hitting the government seat signals the Houthis will widen the war beyond Saudi territory to the Yemeni government itself, raising pressure on the Mokha/Bab el-Mandeb front and on Riyadh to escalate or negotiate.

title: Record Russian drone barrage hits Kirovohrad region during 'energy truce'
summary: Kirovohrad region suffered its largest Russian attack of the war overnight: 360+ drones hit 26 locations, killing three and wounding six (Gov. Andriy Raikovych). Ukraine's air force said 580 drones were launched nationwide, 536 shot down.

analysis.text: Strikes of this scale on infrastructure are the stated reason Kyiv abandoned the energy pause; expect tit-for-tat refinery and grid strikes to resume at pace.

unplaced: Governor reported 26 locations across Kirovohrad region; no single site named.

title: Trump calls Kyiv's refinery strikes a 'disgrace' as EU summit rallies around Zelenskiy
summary: Trump told Newsmax that Ukraine's resumed strikes on Russian refineries are 'a disgrace' that push world oil prices higher. EU leaders hosted Zelenskiy at their Brussels summit on Oct 16, where he sought a 'winter package' of energy, air defence and funding. Ukraine's finance minister puts the unfunded 2027 budget gap at $32.6 billion, excluding about $40 billion in direct military supplies. Putin said the refinery strikes caused 'nothing particularly significant'. A Putin decree dated Oct 15 (No. 738) placed Russian units of Tarkett, Menshen, Ontex, Kappa Rus (Swedish-owned) and a Sonoco-linked packaging firm under temporary state-appointed management.

causes.why: Kyiv's exit from the energy pause and new refinery strikes drew Trump's rebuke
EU leaders object to the US-Russia diesel deal that underpins Washington's pressure on Kyiv

analysis.text: Washington's operative goal is lower pump prices before the Nov 3 midterms; Europe's is keeping Ukraine solvent and lit through winter without dependable US cover. The asset seizures signal that any EU move on frozen Russian state assets will be answered in kind against European companies still inside Russia.

title: Order to throttle Ukraine's Starshield came from inside the White House, sources say
summary: Two US officials and a Western official told Reuters the order to slow SpaceX's military-grade Starshield service for Ukraine came from inside the White House. Ukrainian officials said terminals stopped working on fast-moving objects, degrading drone guidance and interceptor drones; a Ukrainian defence ministry source said they now work at up to 160 km/h. A senior US official said 'no such request was ever made by the president.' Reuters said US officials had earlier threatened to stop sharing missile-launch intelligence; Trump said on Oct 13 that sharing continues.

causes.why: The curbs came as Washington pressed Kyiv to halt refinery strikes after it quit the energy pause

analysis.text: Regardless of who signed off, the effect is calibrated leverage: Washington can dial down enablers Kyiv depends on without a formal aid cut, pressing it to stop refinery strikes that raise US fuel prices.

unplaced: The restriction applied to Starshield service across Ukraine; no single site is named.

title: Russian drones black out Lutsk and Volyn; three killed in Kharkiv
summary: Russian drone strikes on Volyn region, which borders Poland, left 370,000 people without power on Oct 16 (Reuters, citing local authorities); Lutsk lost electricity and city services ran on backup power. Russian drone strikes on Kharkiv killed three people, and DTEK reported emergency power cuts in Kyiv.

causes.why: Same Russian campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure, now reaching the west

analysis.text: Hitting the far west signals that no part of Ukraine's grid is out of reach heading into winter, which strengthens Kyiv's ask in Brussels for air defence alongside money.

title: IEA speeds up emergency stock release, including 20 million+ barrels of diesel
summary: The IEA Governing Board said about 330 million barrels have been released under its March 2026 Hormuz collective action and agreed to accelerate the remaining ~100 million, with over 20 million barrels of diesel 'as soon as possible'. Reuters said 50 million barrels of diesel had been considered. Argus said about half the diesel would come from France (10 million barrels, November to January) and that the Iran war and Ukraine's refinery campaign have curtailed around a third of global diesel exports. European diesel margins fell nearly 2% to $78.67 a barrel on Oct 16.

causes.why: Surging Hormuz attacks cut Gulf crude and product flows
Ukraine's renewed refinery strikes tighten Russian diesel exports

analysis.text: Stock draws buy time, not supply. A 20-million-barrel diesel release is small next to the disruption, and the smaller-than-discussed figure suggests governments are rationing what is left in strategic stocks.

unplaced: IEA Governing Board decision for 32 member states; no event site.

title: US weighs case-by-case sanctions relief for shadow-fleet tankers to cut freight rates
summary: A US official said the administration is discussing lifting sanctions on individual 'dark fleet' tankers so they can be sold to legitimate operators and carry non-sanctioned oil, to lower record freight rates. Kpler tracks about 160 US-sanctioned supertankers, roughly 22% of the commercial fleet, and estimates only about 24 could realistically rejoin trade; it expects 'virtually no impact'. Freight futures fell and WTI's discount to Brent narrowed to about $10.42 from $14.17 earlier in the week. The Energy Department said the move would not help Russia move oil.

causes.why: Hormuz attacks and war-risk premiums drove tanker rates to records

analysis.text: The aim is the midterm pump price, but case-by-case waivers chip at the sanctions architecture on Russia, Iran and Venezuela that Washington built; markets read it as a sign the White House will trade sanctions discipline for cheaper fuel.

unplaced: Policy deliberation in Washington; no event site.

title: Second tanker in a day burns in Iran's declared 'prohibited zone'; Cape Dao sinks
summary: Iran's navy said an unnamed oil tanker that had switched off its tracking systems caught fire in the Gulf of Oman while crossing the zone the IRGC declared prohibited in September; it gave no cause, flag or crew status, and CENTCOM did not immediately comment. Euronews called it the second such incident in 24 hours. The bulk carrier Cape Dao, struck by a projectile on Sept 23, sank on Oct 14. Kpler said intensified Iranian attacks drove Gulf crude flows sharply lower.

causes.why: Continuation of the October campaign against shipping on the Hormuz approaches

analysis.text: Tehran is running a permission regime on the approaches rather than a full closure: transit on Iran's terms is the leverage it is trading against the US blockade of its ports.

unplaced: Iran said only that the tanker was east of the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf of Oman; no position given.

title: Saudi Arabia blames Iran for Houthi escalation; EU-GCC summit in Riyadh postponed
summary: The GCC and the EU postponed indefinitely the second EU-GCC summit set for Oct 24 in Riyadh, citing Houthi attacks and the closure of King Khalid International Airport. Saudi deputy minister Rayed Krimly told reporters Iran is encouraging the Houthi escalation, that the Houthis refused a July meeting in Oman, that Riyadh has not asked for Iranian mediation, and that some Iranian and Houthi capabilities or intelligence come from 'elements in Russia or China'. AP reported at least 19 killed; the coalition said the Riyadh airport was targeted 20 times this month.

causes.why: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and oil sites made the summit unsafe to host
The widening Houthi campaign sharpened Riyadh's public case against Tehran

analysis.text: Riyadh is building the case for more US military help and for keeping Iran's Yemen card inside any US-Iran deal, while keeping its own line to Tehran open. Losing the summit dents the kingdom's safe-hub pitch to investors.

title: CoreWeave debt scare jolts AI trade; Treasuries rally despite hot inflation
summary: Yields on CoreWeave's junk-rated 2031 bonds rose to about 16% and its default-insurance cost to roughly 1,000 basis points (Reuters); the company has about $50 billion of debt (LSEG). Nvidia's Jensen Huang said CoreWeave's finances are improving and no backstop is needed; Nvidia has agreed to buy its unsold capacity through April 2032. South Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 8% and the Nikkei about 5% on Oct 15 before rebounding about 3% and 1.5% on Oct 16. The US 10-year yield fell 10.2bp to 5.086%, its biggest one-day drop in over a year, even as September PPI rose 6.3% year on year against a 5.3% consensus.

causes.why: Energy-driven inflation keeps long yields high, raising financing costs for leveraged AI builders

analysis.text: The AI build-out runs on credit. With 10-year yields above 5%, held up partly by war-driven energy inflation, the most leveraged borrowers crack first. This is where the Hormuz shock meets the AI-compute storyline.

unplaced: Market-wide credit move; no event site.

title: MSCI moves to drop Indonesia from emerging markets; Jakarta stocks suffer worst day since 1998
summary: MSCI proposed reclassifying Indonesia to 'standalone' status, citing ownership opacity and market dysfunction, with consultation until April 2027. Jakarta's benchmark fell 11% to a six-year low after a 30-minute trading halt, and the rupiah slid 0.6% to 18,070 per dollar. UBS estimated about $4 billion of passive outflows and up to $15 billion more from active funds; minister Airlangga Hartarto questioned why MSCI had not raised the step at a meeting in Bangkok this week.

analysis.text: This is a governance verdict on Prabowo-era policymaking, following negative outlooks from Moody's and Fitch. Capital-flight pressure on the rupiah raises the odds Jakarta leans harder on resource nationalism, including nickel, to fund itself.

unplaced: Index-provider decision on the whole market; no event site.

title: Taiwan tracks 8 PLA sorties, all across the median line, plus 9 navy and 7 official ships
summary: Taiwan's defence ministry detected 8 PLA aircraft sorties, 9 PLAN ships and 7 official ships around Taiwan from 6 a.m. Oct 15 to 6 a.m. Oct 16 (UTC+8). All 8 sorties crossed the median line into the northern and southwestern ADIZ.

causes.why: Continued pressure after the post-Lai-speech drills

analysis.text: Fewer aircraft but every sortie across the median line, with coast-guard-type 'official ships' present, fits Beijing's normalisation of pressure rather than a surge.

unplaced: Activity spread across Taiwan's northern and southwestern ADIZ; no single point.

title: Manila rebukes Chinese envoy's 'thinly veiled threat' of force
summary: The Philippine foreign ministry said Ambassador Jing Quan's remark that 'if we want to use force, we may easily win. But no, we will not use force' was a 'thinly veiled threat of the use of force'. Jing also said Manila faced more risk of confrontation if it did not restore suspended military-to-military communications; Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro called Beijing's stance intimidation, and the Chinese embassy said the remarks were taken out of context.

analysis.text: Beijing is pressing Manila to reopen the military hotline on China's terms while US attention is absorbed by Iran and Ukraine; Manila is betting that public pushback costs it little.

unplaced: Exchange of public statements; no event site.

title: Trump waives much of the new Russia sanctions law two days before it takes effect
summary: Trump signed an executive order on Friday night suspending many sanctions, restrictions and duties in the Russia sanctions law Congress passed and he signed in September, telling Congress the pause was in the US 'national interest'. The law gave him power to levy tariffs of up to 100% on the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas, chiefly China and India, and sanctioned senior Russian figures including Putin, Russian financial institutions and the shadow fleet; the BBC said many of those provisions were waived. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it 'an important and truly historic moment'. Zelenskyy said the sanctions 'could have helped enormously'; Democratic Rep. Don Beyer called it a 'surrender to Putin'.

causes.why: The Russian diesel deal set the frame of easing Russia pressure to cut US fuel prices
The waiver followed Trump's open break with Zelenskyy over refinery strikes

analysis.text: The waiver completes a pivot: Washington is now trading Russia pressure for lower fuel prices before Nov 3, after the diesel deal, the energy pause and the Starshield curbs. Secondary tariffs on China and India were also the one tool that could have hit Russian oil revenue hard, so their removal eases pressure on Beijing and Delhi too. Expect Europe to carry more of Ukraine's financing and sanctions burden.

unplaced: Executive order signed in Washington; a policy act with no event site.

title: Putin declares a 'security zone' inside Ukraine non-negotiable; Kremlin says it spans 660 km
summary: Speaking in uniform at a command post, Putin said Russian forces were establishing a 'security zone' in Ukrainian territory adjacent to Russia's border, framed as a response to Ukraine's 2024-25 Kursk incursion, and that Russia does 'not plan to make this a subject for potential peace negotiations'. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the zone spans 660 km, about 70% of it under Russian control, without saying how deep it would reach. It would require land in Sumy and Kharkiv regions, which Russia has not claimed to annex. Russia's military chief told Putin the military had allocated the assets to press its air campaign against Ukraine's energy system.

analysis.text: Moscow is pocketing a new territorial demand outside its four claimed regions while US pressure is aimed at Kyiv, not Russia. Timing it with the sanctions waiver suggests the Kremlin reads Washington as unwilling to impose costs.

unplaced: A planned 660 km border strip in Sumy and Kharkiv regions; no single site named.

title: Russia hits 15 energy sites; more than 1 million lose power and at least 8 are killed
summary: Russian attacks on Oct 16 struck nine regions, killing at least eight people and injuring 60, hitting two shopping centres and cutting power to more than a million people, Ukrainian officials said; the energy ministry said power was later restored to over a million. Two were killed in Kharkiv, two in Kramatorsk and two in Dnipropetrovsk region; drones hit a shopping centre in Rivne (one killed) and a food plant in Volyn (one killed), and torched about 10 trucks at a Kovel customs terminal. Zelenskyy said 15 energy facilities were hit overnight. A strike on Kherson on Oct 17 killed an ambulance driver. The UN monitoring mission said 328 civilians were killed in September, 85% more than a year earlier.

causes.why: Continuation of the same pre-winter campaign against the grid

analysis.text: Russia is racing to break Ukraine's grid before winter while Kyiv's US enablers are degraded; the western strikes near Poland also test EU air-defence resolve.

title: IRGC says supertanker hit a mine in Hormuz as Brent touches $110
summary: Iran's IRGC navy said a tanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of oil struck a mine on Oct 17 while taking an 'unauthorised route' with its positioning systems off, causing a 'massive explosion'; it gave no location, and the ship's identity was not reported. Al Jazeera said three tankers had been reported hit since Friday, one by an RPG fired from a small boat according to UKMTO. CENTCOM's Adm. Brad Cooper said the strait 'is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran'. On Oct 16 Brent settled up 3.7% at $109.86 after touching $110, its highest since May, and WTI rose 3.5% to $101.41. Kpler put Hormuz crude exports at 9.4 million b/d in the week to Wednesday, about 70% of pre-war levels.

causes.why: Escalation of Iran's campaign against ships crossing its declared zone

analysis.text: Mines change the risk math more than missiles: insurers and owners cannot see the threat, so transit may fall even without new attacks. Iran's aim is to make the US blockade of its ports cost the world more than it costs Tehran. Goldman's $120 upside case is in play if flows keep falling.

unplaced: The IRGC gave no position for the tanker, and no maritime authority has confirmed the incident.

title: Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's Hormuz bypass, is intercepted
summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile over Yanbu, the Red Sea terminus of a major oil pipeline, plus two cruise missiles over the Red Sea and three drones over southern Saudi Arabia and Riyadh; initial reports indicated no damage. Saudi deputy minister Rayed Krimly said Iran's support for the Houthis violates the China-brokered 2023 Beijing agreement. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei rejected any role and offered to mediate. The UN Security Council condemned the Houthi attacks on Oct 15. On Oct 17 the coalition said it destroyed two ballistic-missile launch platforms in Saada.

causes.why: Same Houthi escalation against the kingdom, now aimed at its Red Sea export outlet

analysis.text: Yanbu is the escape valve that lets Saudi crude avoid Hormuz. Targeting it signals that the Houthi campaign is aimed at Gulf export capacity, not just Saudi morale, which pairs with Iran's squeeze on Hormuz. Invoking the Beijing deal also puts China on the spot as guarantor.

title: AI selloff gives stocks their worst week since June as oil and yields stay high
summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.09% to 7,659.44 and the Nasdaq 2.15% to 26,140.03 on Oct 16; the S&P lost about 2% on the week and the Nasdaq about 4.5%, while the Dow eked out a weekly gain. CoreWeave fell 11.9% on the day and more than 23% on the week (WSJ). The 10-year Treasury yield ended near 5.10% after hitting about 5.33% following Wednesday's CPI; September import prices rose 1.1% on the month. The VIX rose about 22% to 20.07, the dollar index slipped 0.24% and gold was little changed near $4,189. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave no rate guidance; CME FedWatch showed more than 80% odds of a hold this month.

causes.why: CoreWeave's debt scare kept pressure on AI stocks through the week

analysis.text: Equities are being squeezed from both ends: energy-led inflation keeps long yields above 5%, which punishes the debt-financed AI build-out. The Dow's resilience shows rotation toward energy and value rather than a broad panic.

unplaced: Market-wide move; no event site.

title: Chinese coast guard ships enter Dongsha restricted waters; PLA flies 9 sorties near Taiwan
summary: Two Chinese coast guard vessels, 3301 and 3303, entered restricted waters around Taiwan-controlled Dongsha (Pratas) Atoll at 3:34 p.m. on Oct 16, and Taiwan's Coast Guard sent ships to order them out; the standoff was ongoing when the CGA issued its statement. The CGA said it had run 11 expulsion operations near Dongsha this year. Taiwan's defence ministry separately detected 9 PLA aircraft sorties, 6 PLAN ships and 8 official ships from 6 a.m. Oct 16 to 6 a.m. Oct 17 (UTC+8); 5 sorties crossed the median line.

causes.why: Continued daily grey-zone pressure around Taiwan

analysis.text: Dongsha is Taiwan's most exposed outpost, far closer to Hong Kong than to Taipei. Repeated coast-guard 'law enforcement' patrols build a paper trail of Chinese jurisdiction that could later justify a quarantine without firing a shot.

title: EU-China trade truce adds a rare-earth 'green channel' but leaves Europe dependent
summary: EU trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and Chinese commerce minister Wang Wentao agreed a 16-point list in Beijing on Oct 8-9, including a 'green channel' to speed licences for rare earths and permanent magnets exported to the EU; in return the EU will work to accelerate priority licences for dual-use items going to China. China also committed to halving hybrid and plug-in hybrid car exports to the EU, with the mechanism undisclosed. EU leaders reviewed the deal at their Oct 15-16 summit. Separately, China continues to restrict controlled rare-earth sales to listed US firms; its suspension of the 0.1% foreign-content rule expires Nov 10.

causes.why: The looming Nov 10 expiry keeps rare-earth licensing at the centre of China's trade leverage

analysis.text: Beijing is splitting the West: faster licences for Europe while US firms stay on restricted lists, just as Washington eases Russia sanctions over European objections. Europe gains predictability, not independence; China can still slow approvals at will.

title: Ethiopian forces sweep Tigray to the Eritrean border, raising fears of interstate war
summary: The New Humanitarian reported on Oct 16 that Ethiopian troops and the pro-government Tigray Peace Force militia took control of towns on Tigray's northern border this week as Eritrean forces stationed along the Zalambessa-Fatsi line crossed back into Eritrea, though some Eritrean troops remain inside Tigray. TPLF fighters withdrew deeper into the mountains after swift reversals since the war resumed in late September, and some residents of the regional capital Mekelle welcomed TPF leaders.

analysis.text: The question is whether Addis Ababa stops at the border or pushes on Asmara, possibly toward its long-sought access to the Red Sea. A war there would sit across the Bab el-Mandeb from the Houthi-Saudi fight and could pull in Egypt, Sudan's factions and Gulf patrons.

title: China's 'Justice Mission 2025' drills rehearse a blockade of Taiwan
summary: For two days (Dec 29–30) the PLA ran joint live-fire drills around Taiwan, which Beijing called a 'stern warning' to separatist and 'external interference' forces. ISW assessed that the exercise rehearsed a blockade and counter-intervention, with coast guard ships enforcing it. Beijing tied the drills to what could be the largest-ever US arms sale to Taiwan and to Japanese PM Takaichi's Taiwan remarks. Taiwan said more than 100,000 air travellers were affected.

causes.why: The 2022 encirclement drills set the template that each new exercise extends

analysis.text: Beijing is normalising blockade rehearsals so that a real quarantine would look like routine, and it is pairing military pressure on Taipei with coercion of Tokyo.

unplaced: Drills ran in several zones around Taiwan; there is no single site.

title: US strikes Venezuela and captures Maduro
summary: The United States carried out a 'large-scale strike' on Venezuela early on Jan 3. Nicolás Maduro and his wife were captured and flown to New York to face narco-terrorism charges. Trump said the US would 'run' the country at least temporarily, and said Vice President and oil minister Delcy Rodríguez was willing to work with Washington as acting president.

causes.why: Washington's 2022 energy bargaining failed to move Maduro; in 2026 it switched from bargaining to force

analysis.text: The stated case is narcotics; the real aims look like control of Venezuelan oil and pushing China, Russia and Iran out of the hemisphere. It also made later US threats against Mexico and Cuba credible.

title: Caracas agrees to ship oil to the US under Washington's control
summary: Trump said Venezuela would export up to $2 billion of crude (30–50 million barrels) to the United States, diverting supply from China. Under the deal, the US would market the oil and put the proceeds in US-controlled accounts. Trading houses Trafigura and Vitol began marketing it, and Indian refiners said in late January that they were being offered only small volumes.

causes.why: The raid gave Washington control of the acting government's oil decisions

unplaced: An agreement announced from Washington; no physical site.

title: Iran crushes nationwide protests; thousands killed
summary: Protests that began in late December 2025 over economic hardship turned against the regime and were suppressed under a nationwide internet and phone blackout. The activist group HRANA confirmed 6,221 deaths by Jan 27 and 7,005 by Feb 12, with thousands more under investigation. Trump threatened US strikes if Iran kept killing protesters and sent naval forces to the region.

causes.why: Same pattern: a protest wave met by mass force, deepening the regime's legitimacy gap

analysis.text: The killings gave Washington and Israel a political case and a reading that the regime was brittle, which fed the decision to strike in February.

unplaced: Nationwide protests and crackdown; there is no single site.

title: Yemen's southern separatists announce disbanding as a Saudi–UAE rift opens
summary: After the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council pushed into Hadramaut and al-Mahra in December, a Saudi-backed counteroffensive retook the areas. On Jan 9, STC members in Riyadh announced the council's dissolution. STC leaders called the decision coerced and void, and thousands rallied in Aden on Jan 10 in support of the group.

causes.why: The 2022 council bundled Saudi- and UAE-backed factions; that bargain broke in 2026

analysis.text: Riyadh took sole control of the anti-Houthi camp and sidelined Abu Dhabi's proxy. The same Saudi–UAE split resurfaced in April when the UAE quit OPEC.

title: Congo's army returns to Uvira after M23 withdraws under US pressure
summary: Congolese troops returned to the strategic eastern town of Uvira, near the Burundi border, after M23 rebels withdrew. The pullout followed US pressure linked to the Washington peace accords between Congo and Rwanda.

causes.why: M23's 2022 resurgence began the expansion that reached Uvira

title: Trump drops Greenland tariff threat after European troops deploy
summary: Trump had threatened 10% tariffs, rising to 25% in June, on eight European countries that joined Denmark's Operation Arctic Endurance in Greenland. At Davos on Jan 21 he dropped the tariffs, said he would not use force, and announced a 'framework' on Arctic security after talks with NATO's Mark Rutte. Denmark and Greenland rejected any transfer of sovereignty.

analysis.text: Allies learned that collective pushback works, and also that Washington will use tariffs against NATO members. Both lessons pushed Europe to hedge, including with the India trade deal days later.

title: India and the EU conclude the 'mother of all trade deals'
summary: India and the European Union announced the conclusion of a free trade agreement after nearly two decades of talks, cutting tariffs on a broad range of goods and services. The deal still needs legal vetting and approval in Brussels and New Delhi before it takes effect.

causes.why: US tariff threats against allies pushed both sides to lock in other markets

unplaced: Negotiated deal with no single signing site in the sources.

title: Clashes erupt in Tigray; Ethiopian Airlines halts flights
summary: Fighting broke out between Ethiopian federal troops and Tigrayan forces in western Tigray. Ethiopian Airlines cancelled flights to the region as fears grew of a return to war.
